description: Worker probe:smoke fails with 'auth bootstrap failed — Keycloak unreachable' even though the Keycloak container is healthy. Root cause: stack-up-docker.sh allocates dynamic ports per worker (KEYCLOAK_PORT=37xxx, APP_PROXY_PORT=36xxx) and exports them into docker compose, but the worker's root .env keeps the static boilerplate defaults (9080, 4181) inherited from stack-env-hydrate.sh's copy-from-canonical step. Anything that reads .env via dotenv (pnpm probe:smoke, db:migrate:deploy, integration tests, the API at boot) sees the stale port and tries to talk to 127.0.0.1:9080 which is never published. Builders historically lose entire iterations chasing this as if it were a Keycloak realm/seed bug.
resolution: Two complementary fixes (commit pending in scripts/stack-up-docker.sh + scripts/probe-bootstrap.sh): (1) stack-up-docker.sh upserts KEYCLOAK_PORT, APP_PROXY_PORT, PG_PORT, API_PORT, NEXT_PORT, OAUTH_ISSUER_URL, OAUTH_JWKS_URL, OAUTH2_PROXY_REDIRECT_URL, OAUTH2_PROXY_WHITELIST_DOMAIN, NEXT_PUBLIC_POST_LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URI, NEXT_PUBLIC_OIDC_LOGOUT_ENDPOINT, NEXT_PUBLIC_OAUTH2_PROXY_CLIENT_ID into the worker's .env right after port allocation. Worker-only — canonical app-dev-host .env stays static. (2) probe-bootstrap.sh's hydrate_stack_runtime_env now writes the same values into .env as a safety net so probe:smoke survives even if stack:up was skipped or the .env drifted. Also persists exports to .env.runtime (gitignored) so the next bash subshell in the && pipeline can source them. Both are idempotent and have regression tests in scripts/__tests__/.

description: pnpm probe:smoke is three commands chained with &&: 'bash scripts/probe-bootstrap.sh && pnpm openapi:check && bash scripts/probe-run-with-ownership-check.sh'. Each segment runs in its own bash subshell, so anything probe-bootstrap.sh exports via 'export VAR=...' or 'eval source-runtime-env-file' dies at the first &&. Subsequent segments only see env they read from the OS process env at their own start (pnpm/dotenv-loaded .env, etc.).
resolution: Don't rely on in-process exports across the && chain. Either persist into .env (dotenv picks it up at next pnpm boot) or write to .env.runtime that downstream callers source explicitly. probe-bootstrap.sh now does both.

description: OAuth/Keycloak hostname strategy: SINGLE hostname (keycloak.localtest.me) used by every consumer. The original failure was a builder probe getting tokens with iss=A while the api validated against iss=B; the obvious fix is 'pick whichever hostname both share' but that breaks one of the two consumer classes (browsers OR panel-container probes). Two consumer classes need to reach Keycloak: (a) real browsers from the primary `app-dev-host` stack (humans logging in) — can resolve *.localtest.me via public wildcard DNS to 127.0.0.1, CANNOT resolve Docker-only hostnames like host.docker.internal. (b) server-side processes in containers (api, oauth2-proxy, the SFX panel running probe:smoke against worker stacks) — can resolve hostnames declared in extra_hosts. keycloak.localtest.me is the only hostname that satisfies both classes, so it is the canonical choice.
resolution: Pin OAUTH_ISSUER_URL/JWKS_URL/whitelist on keycloak.localtest.me everywhere. Make every container that needs server-side Keycloak access declare 'keycloak.localtest.me:host-gateway' in extra_hosts: (1) sfx-apps-boilerplate/docker-compose.yml api + app-oauth2-proxy services (regression test in scripts/__tests__/oauth2-proxy-compose.test.mjs). (2) sfx-team-panel/docker-compose.yml panel service (this was the missing piece — panel only had host.docker.internal mapped, so probe:smoke from inside it failed). For an already-running panel without a restart, hot-patch /etc/hosts: docker exec --user root sfx-team-panel-panel-1 sh -c 'echo "$(getent hosts host.docker.internal | awk "{print \$1}") keycloak.localtest.me app.localtest.me" >> /etc/hosts'. Browser-facing redirect URIs use app.localtest.me (also wildcard). Keep host.docker.internal:host-gateway in extra_hosts for Linux portability of non-OAuth tooling (db tunnels, port forwarders).

description: Original probe failure that led to the single-hostname decision (mx-c1a32f). Symptom: probe:smoke gets a valid token from Keycloak but every authenticated request returns 401 'Invalid token issuer'. Root cause was that the panel container had only host.docker.internal in extra_hosts — no keycloak.localtest.me — so probe-bootstrap fell back to host.docker.internal when fetching tokens. Keycloak start-dev mints iss=<request-host>, so tokens carried iss=host.docker.internal:<port> while the api validated against OAUTH_ISSUER_URL=keycloak.localtest.me:<port>. Initial wrong fix was to swap everything to host.docker.internal — worked for probes but broke real-browser logins on the primary stack (Chrome can't resolve Docker-only hostnames). Cost a builder ~70 minutes of looping diagnostics.
resolution: See mx-c1a32f for the right architectural answer. Lesson: when picking a hostname for a service consumed by both real browsers and server-side containers, the candidate hostname must be resolvable from BOTH — wildcard DNS entries (*.localtest.me) plus extra_hosts on every container that needs server-side access. Never use Docker-only hostnames (host.docker.internal) for any URL that ends up in a redirect_uri or token iss claim that a browser will eventually see.

description: @anatine/zod-openapi 2.2.6 cannot extract metadata from .openapi() if it is chained AFTER .optional() or .nullable(). Wrong order compiles cleanly and unit tests on the schema itself pass, but generateSchema(schema) throws TypeError 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading metaOpenApi)' at NestJS module load when @ApiBody/@ApiResponse decorators evaluate, killing the api before it can serve a single request. Symptom in the logs is a stack ending at packages/validation/src/openapi.ts -> generateSchema -> @anatine/zod-openapi/src/lib/zod-openapi.ts:316.
resolution: .openapi() MUST come BEFORE .optional() and .nullable() on every Zod field. Canonical pattern: z.string().openapi({description:'x'}).optional() and z.string().openapi({description:'x'}).nullable().optional(). See packages/validation/src/schemas/common.schema.ts for the reference shape — every existing schema follows this order. If you upgrade @anatine/zod-openapi past 2.2.6, retest both orderings before relaxing this rule.

description: apps/api Dockerfile builds @sfx/domain, @sfx/shared, @sfx/validation, @sfx/database to dist at IMAGE BUILD TIME (development stage). docker-compose.yml bind-mounts only packages/<x>/src into the running container, NOT packages/<x>/dist. Result: when a worker (or any branch) adds a new schema/entity to packages/*/src after the image was built, the running container has src visible but dist still reflects the canonical boilerplate's version — the new export resolves to undefined at @sfx/api boot, surfacing as 'Cannot read properties of undefined' inside whatever decorator first uses the missing export.
resolution: apps/api/package.json dev script now runs `pnpm -r --filter @sfx/domain --filter @sfx/shared --filter @sfx/validation --filter @sfx/database run build` before `nest start -b swc --watch`. Adds ~3-4s to api container boot but guarantees dist matches src on every container start, including after stack:reset/stack:up cycles in worker stacks. The Dockerfile still builds packages at image build time — the dev script is a safety net, not a replacement.

description: stack-up-docker.sh emits '[stack-up] WARN: /etc/hosts is missing host.docker.internal entry' every time pnpm stack:up runs inside the SFX panel container. The warning is a false positive in container context: Docker Desktop and Linux Docker provide host.docker.internal via the container's DNS resolver / extra_hosts mapping, NOT via /etc/hosts. The grep for `^127.0.0.1[[:space:]]+host.docker.internal` in /etc/hosts always fails inside containers, regardless of whether host.docker.internal actually resolves (which it does, via DNS). Probe agents see this warning on every iteration and chase it as if it were a real config gap.
resolution: Gate the /etc/hosts check on `[ ! -f /.dockerenv ]`. The /.dockerenv marker file is created by every official Docker image at build time, so its absence means we're on a real host — exactly the case where the warning IS valid (host browser hitting host.docker.internal:<port> DOES need the /etc/hosts entry, since Docker Desktop only adds host.docker.internal to container DNS, not to the host /etc/hosts). Inside any container the marker is present and the warning is suppressed. Regression test in scripts/__tests__/stack-up-docker.test.mjs asserts the gating expression is in place.

description: CONTRACT_STATUS_UNREACHABLE_UNGENERATABLE on auth-required endpoints had two compounding bugs that pushed agents toward inventing local register/login scaffolds on top of the Keycloak + oauth2-proxy stack. (1) Path-prefix mismatch: diagnostics emit endpoint strings from the OpenAPI source ('GET /api/v1/auth/me'), but curated flow step.path is unprefixed ('/auth/me') because the runtime contract-flow runner (executeCuratedFlows in http-smoke.ts) prepends the API global prefix at execution time. The original buildCoverageSet recorded coverage against the literal step.path, so coveredTuples.has('GET /api/v1/auth/me:200') missed against a curated entry of 'GET /auth/me:200' and the suppression silently failed — leaving UNGENERATABLE for endpoints that ARE covered. (2) Misleading message text: 'Add a declared register/login flow or cover this success path with a curated authenticated flow' put register/login first, which on a Keycloak-backed project with no API-owned credential surface led an agent to build a custom email/password module on top of the existing oauth2-proxy stack.
resolution: Two coupled fixes in flows-generator.js mirrored across all 5 agent profiles (builder/scout/reviewer/lead/merger). (a) buildCoverageSet now accepts an apiPrefix parameter; when set, it emits BOTH the unprefixed step.path tuple AND the prefixed variant so suppression matches regardless of which side of the prefix the comparison runs. The prefix is read from matrix.authDetection.apiPrefix (already populated by matrix-loader). Generated flows pass apiPrefix=null because their step paths already include the prefix. (b) The diagnostic message text now leads with curated-flow + _shared.json guidance (correct for delegated-auth setups), qualifies the register/login suggestion as conditional on the API itself owning the credential surface, and explicitly forbids the @Public() escape hatch. 6 regression tests in .overstory/claude-profiles/builder/hooks/__tests__/flows-generator/flows-generator.test.js cover both fixes (apiPrefix variants, double-prefix protection, normalized leading slash, message-text invariants). 47/49 tests pass; the 2 failing tests are pre-existing on master and unrelated.

description: c33f172 introduced apiPrefix-aware curated coverage in flows-generator.js, reading the prefix from matrix.authDetection.apiPrefix. Validation on a fresh one-shot seed proved the assumption wrong: the persisted .matrix.json had NO authDetection block at all (not even a null apiPrefix — the entire object was missing). The lookup resolved to undefined, buildCoverageSet skipped the prefixed-variant emission, and CONTRACT_STATUS_UNREACHABLE_UNGENERATABLE kept firing for /api/v1/auth/me + /api/v1/version despite curated coverage. Symptom was confusing because the probe still exited 0 (curated flows ran successfully end-to-end with real Keycloak bearers) — only the static diagnostic survived. Root cause: flows-generator.js loads .matrix.json directly via JSON.parse(), bypassing matrix-loader.ts where the `apiPrefix: 'api/v1'` default is applied. Two code paths read the same file with different defaulting semantics.
resolution: f36aa46 adds deriveApiPrefixFromEndpoints(matrix.apiEndpoints) as a structural fallback. The function splits all apiEndpoints[].path on '/' and looks for a consensus leading segment at depth 2 (e.g. 'api/v1') or depth 1 (e.g. 'api'). 80% threshold tolerates outliers like /health and /metrics. Returns null when there's no clear consensus. Lookup precedence is now: (1) matrix.authDetection.apiPrefix explicit, (2) derive from endpoints, (3) null. Anytime you add a new defaulting field to matrix-loader.ts, audit downstream consumers — flows-generator.js, resource-graph.js, http-smoke.ts — to confirm they either go through the loader or carry the same default. 8 regression tests in the boilerplate test suite cover the derivation.

description: On 2026-05-15 a version-builder Stop hook chain stalled for 7+ minutes inside `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and required manual SIGTERM cleanup. Trace: closeout gate re-ran `pnpm probe:smoke` -> `pnpm stack:up` -> `bash scripts/stack-up-docker.sh`. The stack was already healthy (containers Up, /api/v1/health 200), but the script's 'Stack already running (all green)' guard at line 477 missed because docker compose ps returned 0 running services in the brief window the check ran (race against a recent docker compose restart). Control fell through to the install branch where NEEDS_INSTALL=1 fired (a `node_modules/.bin/tsc` symlink was missing in the worktree's pnpm layout) and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline` then hung with no progress. Two layers of damage: (1) a stop hook should never re-boot the stack at all when probe:smoke is run as verification, (2) any pnpm install in the boot path needs a watchdog so a registry/store stall can't masquerade as work.
resolution: Two-layer fix. Layer 1 (probe-bootstrap.sh): added should_skip_stack_up() — when .stack.json exists and `curl http://${stack_host}:${api_port}/api/v1/health` returns any concrete 2xx/4xx code, the script logs '1/6 stack already healthy per .stack.json - skipping stack:up' and bypasses `pnpm stack:up` entirely. Cold probes have no .stack.json so the fast-path is naturally inert. Layer 2 (stack-up-docker.sh): wrapped `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline --config.confirm-modules-purge=false` in `timeout ${STACK_INSTALL_TIMEOUT}` (default 300s). On exit code 124 the script logs an explicit 'pnpm install timed out after Ns - investigate registry / lockfile / pnpm-store' and exits 1, surfacing the hang in seconds instead of holding a builder hostage. Both fixes have regression tests in scripts/__tests__/probe-bootstrap.test.mjs and scripts/__tests__/stack-up-docker.test.mjs that pin the exact wiring (should_skip_stack_up name, /api/v1/health probe, STACK_INSTALL_TIMEOUT env default, 124 exit branch).

description: On 2026-05-15 the F1 brand-profile builder hit the close-gate with 6 CONTRACT_STATUS_UNREACHABLE_UNGENERATABLE rows on GET|PUT|DELETE /api/v1/brands/:id, despite curated coverage in sfx-webapp-boilerplate-b859.json that exercised every status against a real Keycloak-authenticated stack. Coverage tracker emitted tuples like 'GET /api/v1/brands/${brandId}:200' (curated step.path uses template-literal style for runtime binding substitution) but diagnostics emitted 'GET /api/v1/brands/:id:200' (NestJS route-param style from @Get(':id') controllers). The two strings are literal-unequal, so coveredTuples.has(diagKey) missed for every parameterized success path. Earlier f36aa46 fix only handled the apiPrefix dimension; the path-param naming dimension was still asymmetric. The static UNGENERATABLE diagnostic survived even though contract-flows ran 20/20 green and qa-test was 24/24 green — looked like a real coverage gap when in fact the entire chain was working end-to-end.
resolution:
Added canonicalizePathParams(rawPath) to flows-generator.js — replaces both ${anyVarName} (curated template literals) and :paramName (NestJS/Express route markers) segments with a single sentinel

. buildCoverageSet now emits the canonical-shape variant alongside the literal forms (preserves backward-compat exact-match), and the diagnostic-suppression filter checks both literalKey and canonicalKey before deciding to surface UNGENERATABLE. Path SEGMENTS that look like literal values (UUIDs, sentinels like 'non-existent-id', kebab-case slugs) are intentionally NOT canonicalized — they stay literal so 401-style anonymous flows only suppress the matching literal endpoint. 8 regression tests cover the canonicalization (${var} vs :param vs literal, idempotence, edge cases) plus an end-to-end repro of the F1 brand-profile incident. Mirrored across all 5 agent profiles (builder/lead/reviewer/scout/merger). When you add a new dimension to coverage matching (api-prefix, path-param shape, host alias, etc.), audit BOTH sides of the comparison — emission AND suppression — and add a regression test that uses the actual OpenAPI/NestJS-style diagnostic key, not just the curated step shape.

description: Option A for mx-cd88c5 (pre-populate observedTuples from curatedSummary.contract.specialFlows in http-smoke.ts L961+) deploys identically to all 5 profile copies and curated 20/20 PASS at runtime, but CONTRACT_STATUS_UNREACHABLE still fires on /auth/me:200 and /brands:200 — both endpoints have no path params so 928e961 canonicalization is irrelevant. Likely cause: tuple-key form mismatch between observedTuples (built from step.path) and contract-side status-tuples set in checkContractCoverage (built from contract endpoint path). The +31 vs +39 line asymmetry across profiles is an UNRELATED hostname-override block in readStackRuntimeEnvValue L1323+, not the ordering patch.
resolution: Pending operator decision: A' (fix tuple-key build to match contract-side normalization), B (move flows to _shared.json which is excluded from coverage credit per loadCuratedFlowSteps L174), or C (overlay.ignore — likely hook-blocked since path was introduced by diff). Coord recommends B.
